text:
anya: quick q — tuning TTFT/p95 alerts. where do folks slice by model/region and tokens/sec in grafana? trying to stop noisy alerts during rampups

sam: for TTFT dashboards check /d/ttft-overview (p50/p95/p99 by model). there are dropdowns for region and route. panels named "TTFT by model" and "TTFT tail"

devon: quick link i use: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ab12TTFT/ttft-overview?orgId=1 — set var-model and var-region on the top right

sam: promql snippets that help:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_response_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region))
```
and tokens/sec:
```
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model, region)
```
filter with `model=~"your-model-regex"`

lucas: if you want tokens per response:
```
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[1m])) by (model)
```
helps correlate high TTFT with long outputs

maria: alert tuning notes: prefer p95 over p99 for noisy routes. use a rolling window and a burn rate guard. example rule idea:
```
alert: HighTTFT_P95
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_response_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) > 0.25
for: 10m
labels: { severity="page" }
annotations: { runbook="link-to-ttft-runbook" }
```
add a label matcher to skip canary models or add `and on(model) deployment_phase == 0` if we export that metric

ops-bot: deployment-silence: canary windows auto-silenced yesterday for `infra/canary` :thumbsup:

anya: super helpful — i'll try those queries and post the alert rule draft. any tips for debugging a single noisy host?

sam: for host-level: use the trace sample id from the TTFT panel -> open jaeger with `service=inference` and operation `GenerateText`. filter by `model` and `host`. span names: `generate.forward` and `kv.cache.miss` are useful to spot slow paths

devon: also check GPU util + sched spikes on the node: metrics `nvidia_gpu_utilization` and `container_cpu_user_seconds_total` around the TTFT spike time

anya: thanks all — will post back with the draft alert and a couple trace links to review
